title: Canary SLO Gates and Circuit-Breaker Calibration Guidelines
creator: Asha R. Patel
description: This ticket defines a canonical pattern for gating canary rollouts using SLO-based gates and a harmonized circuit-breaker calibration method. It covers measurement windows, burn-rate checks, latency quantile thresholds, hysteresis, and automated rollback criteria. The goal is to reduce bad rollouts (regressions that violate customer-facing SLOs) while allowing safe progressive rollouts for model and runtime changes.
motivation: We have observed several partial rollouts where regressions in tail latency or model quality propagated to production because the canary check was either too coarse (single-avg latency) or lacked a burn-rate check. We need standard, testable canary gates that operate across regions and for model-variant promotions, and an automated, well-calibrated circuit-breaker that protects the control plane and serving runtime during unexpected degradations.
proposed_solution: Introduce a canary gate service that evaluates a small percentage of mirrored/real traffic against a canary deployment for a rolling evaluation window. The gate will evaluate SLI buckets (p50/p95/p99 latency, success rate, model-accuracy surrogate via eval hooks) and burn-rate over short and medium windows (5m and 1h). If any of the configured rules are tripped, the gate will mark the canary as failed and trigger automated rollback. The same metric streams feed a calibrated circuit-breaker component in the ingress layer that uses quantile-aware thresholds and a token-bucket style admission policy for graceful shedding.
metrics_and_sli_definitions:
Primary SLIs to evaluate canaries: p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, request_success_rate (status code & internal error map), model_quality_eval_pass_rate (periodic small eval set), token_drop_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate. SLO expressions used in gating:
- Latency SLO: p95_latency_ms <= 250ms (gold tier route)
- Tail SLO: p99_latency_ms <= 500ms
- Availability SLO: request_success_rate >= 99.5%
- Quality SLO: model_quality_eval_pass_rate >= 98% (only for model variant canaries)
Each SLI must be computed with the same aggregation window as the canary evaluation window and annotated with sample counts and confidence intervals. Burn-rate will be computed relative to the configured SLO over the same windows (see burn-rate thresholds below).
burn_rate_policy:
Two-window burn-rate checks: short_window = 5 minutes, medium_window = 60 minutes. Compute error budget consumption rate r = (SLO_target - observed) / SLO_target normalized to time. Trigger conditions:
- Immediate abort: r_short >= 3.0 sustained for >= 3 consecutive 1-minute sub-windows OR p99 exceeding absolute hard limit (e.g., 1s)
- Fail-canary (non-automated): r_short in [1.2, 3.0) OR r_medium >= 1.5
- Allow-canary (pass): r_short < 1.0 and r_medium < 1.0.
Notes: thresholds are intentionally conservative for gold-tier routes and can be tuned per route class.
circuit_breaker_specification:
State machine: CLOSED -> normal flow; OPEN -> drop or redirect to fallback variants; HALF_OPEN -> allow probe traffic at controlled rate.
Open criteria (ingress level):
- error_budget_burn_rate (global route) > 5.0 for 2 minutes OR p99_latency > 2x SLO for 1 minute OR request_success_rate < 95% for 3 minutes.
Probe strategy for HALF_OPEN: allow 1% of previous baseline QPS as probes for 30s; if probes meet SLO on both short and medium windows, transition to CLOSED with staged ramp-up (25%, 50%, 100% over configurable period).
Hysteresis and cooldown: min_open_duration = 120s; cool_down_after_close = 300s where circuits cannot re-open unless errors exceed a higher reopen threshold.
Shedding policy: prioritize shed candidates by route priority then model_variant_weight; shed at token-count granularity where possible. Admission uses a token-bucket with dynamic refill based on observed healthy capacity.
canary_workflow:
1) Create canary with traffic mirroring at 1% of production QPS for 10 minutes. 2) Run automated eval hooks (synthetic prompts) in parallel to measure model_quality_eval_pass_rate. 3) Continuous SLI sampling with 10s granularity, computed over the 5m rolling window and 1h window. 4) If canary passes short-window and medium-window checks, ramp to 10% traffic for 30 minutes, then 50% for 1 hour, then full promotion. 5) Any fail condition triggers immediate rollback; if safe to do so, the system will route yellow traffic to fallback variant while investigating.
Traffic shaping: initial mirror -> canary mirrored + 1% live; mirrored traffic is tagged and cost-accounted. Canary rollouts must be tracked in the release dashboard and have a human override flag for "force promote" with explicit approval and recorded justification.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: implementation of gate evaluator and metric plumbing (2 sprints). Phase 1: pilot on low-risk routes (non-gold routes) with manual review (1 sprint). Phase 2: enable automated rollback for pilot routes and tune thresholds (2 sprints). Phase 3: roll out to gold routes with finalized thresholds and documented runbooks (1 sprint). Backstop: emergency kill switch in global router.
monitoring_and_alerts:
Dashboards: canary-health (per-canary SLI timeseries), circuit-breaker-state (counts per route/region), burn-rate-alerts. Alerts:
- P0: canary_aborted_automated with link to runbook if immediate rollback occurs.
- P1: burn_rate_exceeded_short_window (5m) when r_short >= 1.5.
- P2: circuit_breaker_opened_for_route.
All alerts include sampling links to raw traces, sample requests, and recent PRs touching routing/canary code path. Instrumentation tasks: ensure request-level metadata includes canary_id, model_variant, region, route_priority, and token_count.
acceptance_criteria: Canary gate evaluates SLIs continuously and records decisions in the release dashboard
Automated rollback triggers on defined immediate abort conditions and performs safe traffic reversion
Circuit-breaker transitions (CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN) observed in a simulated test and follow the cooldown/hysteresis rules
Probe traffic mechanism in HALF_OPEN is implemented and validated via load tests
Runbook documented with exact escalation steps and observed in two on-call drills
Unit and integration tests for gate logic, burn-rate math, and state transitions added to CI
open_questions: Should the default canary mirror window be 5m or 10m for low-traffic routes?
What is the canonical list of gold-tier routes (affects thresholds)? Proposal: routes labeled 'gold' in routing-config. Need PM confirmation.
How to surface model_quality_eval_pass_rate for black-box third-party models where internal eval hooks are slower? Consider asynchronous gating with longer windows.
Should we expose a per-team override to loosen thresholds for experimental features? Requires audit trail and TTL.
Operationally, who approves forced promotions if automated gate fails but owner asserts safety? Define approval quorum.
